proposed_destinations.name: Launceston
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a 'Launceston' city chapter, the launceston.com.au tourism board uses the name; 117,274 page views.
proposed_destinations.note: Second-largest Tasmanian city, base for the northeast and the Tamar. Rank 1-2 not claimed; 9 kept spots.

proposed_destinations.name: Tamar Valley
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: centre of its spots (Beaconsfield, Beauty Point, Low Head, George Town); a region centre, not a source point
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a 'Tamar Valley' regional page (en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tamar_Valley); the 'Tamar Valley Wine Route' is a tourism-board brand. Not a council or river grouping: travellers say they are going to the Tamar Valley.
proposed_destinations.note: Launceston is 33 km from the centre and its own destination; Tamar Valley is a separate day-trip or overnight base (Beauty Point, Low Head). Only Tamar Island Wetlands, Tasmania Zoo and Brady's Lookout sit in the shared zone: the first two are Launceston's, Brady's is on the river.

proposed_destinations.name: Bay of Fires
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: centre of its spots (Binalong Bay, St Helens, Eddystone Point, Mount William NP); a region centre, not a source point
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Wikipedia 'Bay of Fires' (18,178 page views) and Parks Tasmania/Wikivoyage 'St Helens (Tasmania)' chapter name the Bay of Fires as the headline attraction; the region is the Bay of Fires and St Helens tourism brand. Wikivoyage has no standalone Bay of Fires page (404), so the headline-attraction route to the name test is used. Region over the town per COVERAGE 'Prefer the region travellers name'.
proposed_destinations.note: Named for the region not St Helens (whose draws are the bay, Mount William and Pyengana). Ben Lomond (65 km) is not part of it.
